summary: The AssaultRunner Pro is the primary treadmill used to develop and test RunBridge.
evidence: Inventory compatibility record marked compatible; original treadmill used to develop RunBridge.
setup: Power on the console and start a treadmill session so live FTMS workout data is available.
limitations: A customer console variant used an additional FTMS flag and required a firmware parsing correction now included in version 4.0.1.

publicStatus: Confirmed with lab and customer evidence
summary: The Spirit XT685 is recorded as compatible after Spirit-specific Bluetooth and FTMS handling was added to RunBridge firmware.
evidence: Inventory record is marked compatible and cites both lab and customer evidence; firmware history documents XT685 notification, control-point, and packet parsing corrections.
setup: Start the treadmill belt when prompted; some Spirit consoles do not stream workout packets while stationary.
limitations: Older firmware may not include the Spirit-specific Bluetooth library and parsing corrections.

summary: The Horizon 7.4 AT is recorded as compatible with firmware handling for its alternating FTMS packets.
evidence: Inventory record is marked compatible; firmware history documents the 7.4 AT zero-value alternating packets, pace-source flipping, and distance drift corrections.
setup: Use current RunBridge firmware so alternating FTMS packets are handled correctly.
limitations: Earlier firmware could interpret alternating zero-value packets as motion stops.

summary: A customer deployment of the Darwin TM30 is recorded as compatible with RunBridge firmware 4.0.1.
evidence: Inventory compatibility record is explicitly marked compatible for a customer deployment using firmware 4.0.1.
limitations: Console revision and detailed FTMS characteristics were not recorded.
